title: Compact density: semantic swatches and elevation recalibration for compact components
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: our existing token set was optimized for default density and medium contrast, which causes cramped tables and noisy charts when users opt into compact layouts. Several teams reported inconsistent hover/focus emphasis and flattened elevation on dense dashboards.

Goal: introduce a compact-density token subset and recalibrate semantic swatches, typography scale, spacing steps, radius tokens, and elevation layers so compact components (tables, buttons, charts, list items) maintain accessible contrast, clear affordances, and consistent rhythm at smaller sizes.

Scope:
- Color: add semantic accent variants for compact interactive states (+hover/+active/+focus), a condensed neutral ramp for compact surfaces, and a distinct chart palette tuned for small markers.
- Typography: tighten the scale for compact mode (12/13/14/16/18) and document variable-font fallbacks and recommended line-heights.
- Spacing & radius: introduce a compact spacing scale (4/6/8/12) and small-radius tokens (r-xs, r-sm) to preserve tap targets while reducing visual bulk.
- Elevation & shadow: redefine 4 elevation steps for compact surfaces ensuring contrast with adjacent layers and fewer, crisper shadows to avoid visual clutter.

Non-goals: full global redesign; this is an additive compact token layer that maps to existing component styles with migration tokens for compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens exported to main token JSON with compact.* namespace (e.g., compact.space-4, compact.radius-xs)
Figma library updated with compact variants for Button, Table row, Card, and Chart components
Front-end playground demonstrates compact toggle across at least: Buttons, Tables, Lists, Line/Bar/Scatter charts
Automated visual diff baseline created and attached; no regressions for default-density snapshots
Accessibility checks: contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for body text in compact lists; focus rings visible at 3:1 with additional offset guidance

notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive radius reduction improves density but can reduce perceived tap affordance; chosen compromise: two compact radius tokens (r-xs=4px, r-sm=6px) with explicit touch-target guidance.
- Fewer elevation layers reduces visual noise but increases reliance on color separation; we paired elevation adjustments with subtle neutral ramp changes to maintain surface separation.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add compact tokens alongside existing tokens (no breaking changes). Update Figma components to include compact variants.
Phase 2: Implement CSS var mapping and add compact toggle to Console settings for beta customers.

Phase 3: Run A/B with Platform teams, collect metrics (error rates, perceived density satisfaction), and finalize naming. Deprecate legacy dense tokens in two releases after migration shims are removed.
